thread.title: New 44-Acre Town Center Proposed

author: Teresa Pearson
title: New 44-Acre Town Center Proposed
text:
Medford- A proposed town center near Hillcrest Road and North Foothill Road could bring shops, housing, a public plaza, and new pedestrian connections to nearly 44 acres in northeast Medford.
Cogswell Limited Partnership is seeking approval to divide the 43.81-acre property at 3285 Hillcrest Road into 21 lots and two reserve acreage tracts. The Hillcrest District Town Center subdivision would proceed in three phases.
The applicant is requesting up to five years to complete the subdivision phases. That request concerns the land division process and does not establish a completion date for buildings or businesses.
A planned 1.1-acre town plaza would provide a gathering place surrounded by future shops, restaurants, and offices. Shared parking areas are proposed on either side. Final plaza and parking designs would require additional approval before commercial development of the surrounding lots.
The application also identifies a future multifamily or senior housing proposal called “Affinity at Medford,” by Inland Group, for an approximately 8.7-acre parcel. That housing project would require a separate application and review.
Plans call for four new commercial streets and extensions of Spring and Judson streets. Along Spring Street, the developer proposes 12-foot sidewalks with tree wells, providing space for outdoor seating and street furnishings.
An “Orchard Row” linear park and shared pedestrian and bicycle trail are proposed along the west side of Bemis Parkway.
The current application establishes lots and infrastructure rather than approving individual buildings or tenants. According to the applicant’s documents, the subdivision itself would not trigger additional off-site traffic improvements. Transportation requirements and sewer capacity would be addressed as specific projects are proposed.
The city’s Land Development Committee is scheduled to review the proposal Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 9:30 a.m. via Zoom.
The meeting allows applicants, city staff, and outside agencies to discuss infrastructure, development standards, and review procedures. Public comment is not taken during the meeting.
Residents can submit written comments or request information through the Medford Planning Department at planning@cityofmedford.org or 541-774-2380.
The proposal remains subject to city review. If approved and developed, it could substantially change the area’s mix of housing, businesses, and public gathering spaces.
